situation (example wording): "How many homicides in Memphis in 2023?", "Homicide victims in Detroit by age", "firearm homicides in NYC in 2024", "all homicides in Memphis in 2023" (the word "homicide" or "murder")
what the app does today: NIBRS homicide counts 09A, 09B and 09C and says so (Jeff 2026-11-25: "NIBRS homicide offenses are 09A/B/C and should say so"). Murder is 09A only. Crime Index homicide is the murder count; Homicide Reports is unchanged.
proposed behavior: "Murder" means murder and non-negligent manslaughter on every source. "Homicide" depends on the source that answers: on Crime Index (Current Trends and Historical) it is the murder count, worded "murders", with no disclaimer and no decline, including for "all homicides"; on NIBRS it is murder and non-negligent manslaughter (09A), negligent manslaughter (09B) and justifiable homicide (09C), and the answer says so ("Homicides here include murder and nonnegligent manslaughter, negligent manslaughter and justifiable homicide."); on Homicide Reports it is murder plus negligent manslaughter, and justifiable homicide is left out unless the question says "all homicides", when the answer states what it counted.
exact default or choices offered: Murder: 09A (Homicide Reports type A). Homicide: 09A, 09B and 09C on NIBRS ("all homicides" is the same set); 09A plus 09B (types A and B) on Homicide Reports; the murder count on Crime Index. Crimes against persons stays without 09C (Jeff 2026-11-25: "no on 09C, yes apply to state and national"); state and national homicide is the murder series, the same as cities.
why: One row says what each word means on each source, so the same question is not read two ways.
status: Decided 2026-11-16 (Jeff); NIBRS homicide changed to 09A/B/C on 2026-11-25 (Jeff). Replaces the 2026-10-28 and 2026-11-06 decisions
test cases: Tests that cite this row: scripts/test-nibrs-shadow.ts, scripts/test-answer-eval-runner.ts, scripts/test-nibrs-plan-language.ts.
